scoring_justification: Full recompute (T1) is infeasible because it would require re-running a complex free-energy minimization with many Fourier harmonics inside the verifier sandbox. The paper provides precise reference values for the two required quantities at the given conditions, so a T0 result-level comparison with tolerances is the strongest feasible tier.

outputs.description: Equilibrium stripe period in nanometers at T=700 K, t=24.2 nm, case I boundary conditions.
Transition temperature Tc in Kelvin for the same film thickness and boundary condition.

output_contract.notes: The checker compares the submitted values against hidden reference numbers using predefined tolerances. Both unitless numeric values are deterministic physical quantities derived from the specified conditions and the LGD theory.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference equilibrium stripe period for t=24.2 nm, T=700 K, case I
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 6 caption; the paper reports d≈13.2 nm for this condition (nonlinear LGD solution).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's reported result: 13.2 nm is the equilibrium stripe period at 700 K for a 24.2 nm PbTiO3 film with symmetric SrTiO3 boundaries (case I).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The number is the exact value the paper states for the same system and conditions as the reproduction task.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference transition temperature Tc for t=24.2 nm, case I
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 10; reading the curve for t=24.2 nm (case I, nonlinear) gives Tc≈963 K. The reference solve.sh writes 963.0 K.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's Fig. 10: for a 24.2 nm PbTiO3 film with case I boundaries, the ferroelectric transition temperature is approximately 963 K. The checker uses this as the target with ±10 K tolerance.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: It is the paper's reported Tc for the specified film thickness and boundary condition, making it the correct comparative reference.
